event: It is Firstday; Nala wakes with Elowen asleep on her arm, her arm numb, and stays still anyway.
Elowen wakes, remembers the kiss, and goes pink, and then kisses Nala again, quickly.
They dress in the narrow room, bumping elbows, laughing under their breath.
On the landing Wren is waiting, and looks from one flushed face to the other.
Wren says only that porridge won't wait, and goes down first, two steps at a time.
At porridge Nala's purse is empty, and so is Elowen's; Wren has two pennies.
Wren grips her spoon, the banister, the table edge, and says her arm is right again.
Wren says the first level is picked over near the gate; they should try the second.
Wren says a copper party of three may go as far as the third level, so it is allowed.
Elowen goes pale; Nala's stomach turns over, and she nods.
The guild's second-level map costs three pennies, and between them they have two.
Nala says she will draw the second level herself as they go, on the back of her map.
Wren laughs and says that makes Nala the party's cartographer.
The warden signs them into the Mouth book, a party of three, second level.
They walk the Long Hall past Elowen's arrows and on past the Well Room to the Dry Stair.
They go down the Dry Stair, broad steep steps worn hollow, colder with every step.
At the bottom the air turns damp; water seeps down the walls and pools on the floor.
Nala stops at every turning to draw the passage onto the back of her map with chalk.
Pale mushrooms glow faintly on the wet walls; Elowen knows them at once as gloomcaps.
Elowen says apothecaries on Coppergate buy them fresh, a penny for six, for sleeping draughts.
She picks them carefully into her herb pouch as they go.
Wren tells them the dangers: blind white lizards as long as an arm hunt in the water.

pictured.coverAfter: It turns damp. Wet. It smells of stone and water and something green.
pictured.setting: the wet passage at the foot of the Dry Stair, second level

event: Their bite festers, Wren says; keep out of deep water and watch the surface.
The passage opens into the Drowned Hall, wide, its floor under knee-deep clear cold water.
Their lamps light the water to the bottom, and the cold of it makes them gasp wading in.
In a heap of fallen stone at the hall's edge Wren finds an ember-stone the size of a walnut.
Wren says the second level's stones are bigger, and the market pays four pennies each.
They search the hall's edges and fallen stone, wet to the knees, numb-footed.
Nala finds one, then another; Elowen finds one wedged in a crack above the waterline.

event: Elowen fills her pouch with gloomcaps until she has eighteen.
Nala sees a ripple in the water, moving against the current, toward Elowen's legs.
She shouts; a long white lizard surges up out of the water at Elowen.
Elowen calls her light blazing white; the lizard is blind, and keeps coming.
Nala grabs Elowen by the arm and hauls her back, and stabs down at the lizard with her knife.
The knife skids off its back and cuts it; the lizard twists away and vanishes into the water.
Elowen stands shaking in the knee-deep water with her light still burning on her fingers.
Wren splashes over, white-faced, and checks Elowen's legs for a bite; her skin is whole.
Wren tells Nala she did well, then says they are getting out of the water, now.
They climb onto a dry ledge at the edge of the Drowned Hall, and Nala's hands start shaking.
Elowen holds Nala's shaking hands in hers until they stop.
They keep to the dry edges after that, and Wren finds a fifth walnut stone in a fallen wall.
Nala draws the Drowned Hall onto her map, and marks where the lizard came up.
Wren studies Nala's chalk map by lamplight and says it is clearer than the guild's.
They climb the Dry Stair, walk the Long Hall by Elowen's arrows, and sign out of the Mouth book.
At the finds market the ember-stone dealer pays four pennies each for the five stones: twenty.
She holds back two pennies for the guild's tenth and pays them eighteen.
Wren splits it on the counter: six each.
At an apothecary's shop on Coppergate Elowen sells her eighteen gloomcaps for three pennies.
She gives one penny each to Nala and Wren, and keeps one.
Nala has seven pennies, the first coin in her purse since the rent.
Wren twists half her share into a scrap of cloth for Saltby.
At the Brass Kettle they each pay four pennies for supper; Nala has three pennies left.
They eat at the corner table, damp to the knees, too tired to talk at first.
Wren asks Nala, lightly, whether there are lizards in Fennick.

event: Nala puts her spoon down, and decides to tell them some of the truth.
Nala tells them Fennick is a blank to her; her memory of this life begins in room 7.
She says she woke there on Fourthday with a pack, a letter and a name stitched in the flap.
Elowen takes her hand under the table and holds it hard.
Wren says that explains a lot: not knowing ember-stones, not knowing the Deep.
Wren admits she could not say where Fennick even is; few up here could, so it will rarely come up.
Nala keeps the rest to herself: Alan, the window, the book open on his chest.
Wren says the party knows now, and that is enough.
Wren walks them up Ladder Lane, between them, an arm through each of theirs.
On the top landing, Elowen goes into room 7 first, and Wren holds Nala back a moment.
Wren asks, quietly, if it is Nala and Elowen now.
Nala says yes, and feels there is more to say, and keeps it for when she has the words.
Wren says Elowen is good, and Nala should be good to her, and her voice catches once.
Nala reaches for Wren's hand; Wren squeezes hers back, hard, then goes into room 8.
In room 7 Elowen is waiting in the narrow bed, holding the blanket open for her.
They lie face to face, and Elowen thanks her for hauling her out of the water.
They kiss, longer than last night, and Elowen's hand rests on Nala's waist.
Nala falls asleep with Elowen against her, thinking of Wren's voice catching on the landing.
A day in Emberdeep ends.
